humanities_role_explanation: Evaluates disciplinary academic and professional competence across specialized humanities subjects including history, philosophy, world religions, jurisprudence, and professional law, designed to test domain-specific knowledge.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: The benchmark is text-only, consisting of text-encoded multiple-choice questions (with LaTeX for mathematical expressions) spanning 57 subjects.
analytical_tasks_explanation: The benchmark utilizes multiple-choice questions to evaluate factual recall of declarative knowledge, logical and quantitative reasoning (e.g., formal logic, mathematics), causal and temporal reasoning (e.g., historical events), and normative judgment (e.g., moral scenarios, legal ethics).

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Evaluates LLM performance across 57 distinct academic and professional subjects spanning STEM, humanities, social sciences, and other areas.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates GPT-3 (various sizes including Ada, Babbage, Curie, Davinci) and UnifiedQA.

quantitative_metrics.note: Evaluates performance using multi-class classification accuracy (%) and root mean squared (RMS) calibration error.

published_after_march_2023.note: Published at ICLR 2021, preprinted in January 2021.

summary: This paper introduces the Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) benchmark, designed to evaluate a model's academic and professional capabilities across 57 diverse subjects. The test is constructed to assess pretraining knowledge exclusively in zero-shot and few-shot settings, shifting the focus of NLP evaluation from basic commonsense to specialized, domain-specific academic knowledge.
key_findings: The largest GPT-3 model (175B) achieved an average few-shot accuracy of 43.9%, substantially above random chance (25%) but far below the estimated human expert baseline (~89.8%). Highly procedural STEM subjects and value-aligned subjects like moral scenarios and professional law proved to be particularly difficult for LLMs, and models demonstrated poor calibration.
review_notes: Minor disagreement on relevant_asjc_areas. Included 'Law' as it is explicitly covered by specific tasks (e.g., Professional Law, Jurisprudence, International Law), but dropped Cip's addition of 'Language and Linguistics' as it is not one of the 57 benchmark subjects. Adopted Cip's expanded benchmark name for completeness.
facets_explanation: The reference answers were obtained directly from pre-existing answer keys of standardized practice exams (such as the GRE, AP exams, and USMLE), undergraduate course materials, and academic textbooks. Because these multiple-choice questions evaluate factual, procedural, and academic knowledge in a closed-book format, correct answers require external domain knowledge not found in the question stimulus itself. The paper does not address annotator disagreement or plurality of readings, relying instead on the absolute correctness of the authoritative source keys.
